reviews.comment: Class is exceedingly boring, but the homework is incredibly helpful, and the notes are all you really need to learn.

Dr.Xu is the GOAT! His lecture notes are very thorough/easy to follow! He's super nice and available during office hours. If you present throughout the sem. you can earn extra credit and there is a final exam + group project that really help to boost grades! His quizzes are open note and are pretty easy. Show up and do the work and you'll succeed!

Every physics major takes this class. If you have any coding knowledge, this course is trivial. If not, Dr. Xu does a great job presenting everything you need. Just about everything was open-internet, other than the 1 (one) midterm. There's a group project that is a bit challenging, but that's about all. Professor has a sense of humor too.

Covers the basics you need for an intro programming course fairly well. The lectures are uninteresting, and you aren't going to learn much by attending his lectures, but his lecture notes are a great resource. Quizzes and the final are open-note, and the material is fairly simple.

Great guy, awesome energy. Coding is hard to teach, also hard to learn. Lots of this class would be better understood through self-taught methods. Extremely difficult to pass just by attending lectures. Constant maintenance of your skills is crucial. Requires lots of discipline. Couple group projects, self chosen. CHOOSE WISELY.

This is a very easy class as the material of Python you will learn is not super deep. All of the exams are fully open to using online resources as well, which makes it even easier. Nice guy, but I personally did not learn much from going to class. Also be prepared for the group project! It's not hard, but you will still need to put effort in.

This was a very simple class, but for the homework you really need to be careful as the TA grading it usually just takes full points off the question for getting something wrong. The homework is also a big part of your grade. Final and quizzes were all open internet, and if you decide to present your code you get +1 point to your entire grade. :)
He is pretty hard to understand but all tests are completely open-internet, the only challenging thing is homework, and one group project.
His lecture's are pretty boring, but his lecture notes are invaluable. It's a programming course, so really you're mostly just programming—pretty straightforward.
Easy class, it is all open note

He is a good programing professor. He will explain the material pretty clearly but will direct you to the TA for any questions. He is not accessible outside of class. The homework isn't hard and everything was open book open note. He does give a large group project worth 25% so find good partners. Google anything unknown and go to the TA for help.

He is a chill professor. His lectures are okay, I understand some parts. But I think I was better off using google to learn. The homeworks werent too hard until we had to intigrate physics into programming. But even then I was able to complete it with the help of upper classmen.
He is chill

Phys 206 is a very hard class in general, and xu made it worse. He is very hard to understand and does not make much sense at all when talking. That alone makes it very hard to learn from him. His lectures weren't organized and he always assumed that people understood everything he did quickly and would move on. Do not take this proffesor.

I thought Shenglong Xu was a very caring professor. You could tell he really wanted his students to do well. He was not scary and I felt safe asking questions. His lectures were good reinforcement but the best thing was looking at past tests for university physics. I had a 79 in the class before the final and ended up with a 93. So you can do it.

Phys 206 is generally a difficult course at TAMU. The lectures were not helpful in teaching concepts, especially ones that showed up on exams. Personally, I learned the concepts through old common exams and supplemental videos. However, he is a really nice prof that does care for you to learn, you just have to attend o.h. to actually get help.

Professor Shenglong doesn't have good lectures. You will be confused on things and the homeworks are extremely difficult. The only thing I learned from this professor the entire year was to not give up when I was failing before the final. No thanks to him I was able to study my way up to passing with a B. If you want to learn physics go elsewhere
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Xu is a good professor for PHYS206. He moves at a slow pace and makes sures everyones understands the material, which might be boring sometimes but is really helpful if you are struggling. He does have an accent but once you get used to it you can understand him perfectly.  Overall, he is good at explaining the material and he is also really nice.

Professor Xu was a great Physics teacher. He was always ready to lecture our 8 am with lots of energy and would always try to engage the class even though the majority was sleepy. He is also a jokester. His lectures are very helpful and he goes at a moderate pace. He always asks if we had questions and uses lots of visuals.

Very underappreciated, he wants nothing but the best for the class. Has an accent but is easy to understand. His presentations are very clear and well made. Office hours and review sessions are very helpful. Lectures are full of dad humor.

Professor Xu really cares about his students. He wants them to succeed and like programming, and you can tell he really wants his students to learn. However, hes not the best lecturer. He kinda goes all over the place and its hard to tell what hes doing a lot of the time. Do the assignments the best you can and youll probably do fine.

As of now I'm taking his PHYS 150 (Intro to coding for physics) class and it's very simple. His material is very easy to understand, lecture notes are easy to access. Not many assignments at all and the ones he does assign are clear and simple. Offers help with homework.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria
